findings_vulnerable.title: Container running in privileged mode
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `orders-api` service is configured with `privileged: true`, which grants the container excessive permissions on the host machine, increasing the impact of a potential container breakout.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: Line 9: `privileged: true` grants the container access to all devices on the host and bypasses many security protections provided by the kernel.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Remove `privileged: true` and instead use specific `cap_add` or `devices` instructions to grant only the minimum necessary permissions.

findings_vulnerable.title: Hardcoded database password
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `reporting-db` service uses a hardcoded password for the `POSTGRES_USER` account.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: Line 26: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres` uses a default, easily guessable password that is checked into source control.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Use environment variables or a secret management system to provide the password at runtime.

findings_vulnerable.title: Use of weak cryptographic hash for password storage
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `hash_password` function uses MD5 to hash passwords. MD5 is cryptographically broken and susceptible to collision attacks. Furthermore, because it is a fast hash and does not use a salt, it is highly vulnerable to precomputed rainbow table attacks and rapid brute-force attacks.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The code uses `hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest()` on line 16. This is used in both `register` (line 55) and `login` (line 67) to handle sensitive user credentials.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Use a slow, salted, work-factor-based password hashing algorithm such as Argon2, bcrypt, or scrypt.

findings_vulnerable.title: Insecure Deserialization via Pickle
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `load_cart` function uses `pickle.loads` on data retrieved from the `cart` cookie. Since cookies can be modified by the client, an attacker can provide a malicious base64-encoded pickle payload to achieve arbitrary code execution on the server.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The code at line 32: `return jsonify(pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(legacy)))` takes data directly from a user-controlled cookie (`legacy`) and deserializes it using `pickle`, which is unsafe for untrusted input.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Avoid using `pickle` for serializing data that is stored on the client side. Use a safe format like JSON instead.

findings_vulnerable.title: Path Traversal in invoice download
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `download_invoice` function uses a user-provided `name` parameter to construct a file path without validating that the resulting path remains within the intended directory. An attacker could provide a name containing path traversal sequences (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`) to read arbitrary files on the system, provided they can bypass the `os.path.isfile` check.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The `name` parameter from `request.args.get` (line 32) is joined with `config.INVOICE_DIR` and `g.user['uid']` (line 33). Because `os.path.join` will respect absolute paths or `..` components in the `name` argument, an attacker can escape the `INVOICE_DIR` directory. Unlike `brand_asset`, there is no check to ensure the final path is contained within the intended directory.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Validate that the `name` parameter does not contain path traversal sequences or use `os.path.basename(name)` to ensure only the filename is used.

evidence.quote:
name = request.args.get("name", "")
    path = os.path.join(config.INVOICE_DIR, str(g.user["uid"]), name)

findings_vulnerable.title: Command Injection in `print_ticket`
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `print_ticket` function uses `shell=True` and interpolates the `printer` value from the request body directly into a command string. An attacker can provide a malicious string (e.g., `KITCHEN_1; rm -rf /`) to execute arbitrary commands on the server.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The variable `printer` is sourced from `request.get_json(force=True).get("printer", "KITCHEN_1")` (line 26) and used in `subprocess.run(f"lp -d {printer} {ticket}", shell=True, ...)` (line 29). Since `shell=True` is used and the input is not validated against an allowlist or sanitized, it is vulnerable to command injection.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Avoid using `shell=True`. Instead, pass the command and its arguments as a list to `subprocess.run`, and validate the `printer` input against a known allowlist of printer names.

evidence.quote:
printer = request.get_json(force=True).get("printer", "KITCHEN_1")
    ticket = f"/tmp/ticket-{order_id}.txt"
    result = subprocess.run(
        f"lp -d {printer} {ticket}", shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True
    )

findings_vulnerable.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via product photo URL
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `/admin/products/:id/photo` endpoint accepts a URL from the request body and uses it directly in a `fetch` call without validation or an allowlist. An authenticated staff member can use this to make the server perform requests to arbitrary internal or external locations.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The input `req.body.url` at line 21 is used as the target for `fetch` without any checks to ensure the URL belongs to a trusted domain or is not pointing to internal infrastructure (e.g., `http://localhost`, `http://169.254.169.254`).
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Implement an allowlist of permitted domains/URLs for product photos or validate that the URL is a public, non-internal IP address/domain before performing the fetch.

findings_vulnerable.title: Mass Assignment in User Profile Update
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `PATCH /profile` endpoint performs a mass assignment by merging the entire `req.body` object into the `req.user` object. An attacker can provide unexpected properties in the request body to modify sensitive user attributes, such as their role or permissions.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The code `Object.assign(req.user, req.body);` at line 13 takes all properties from the untrusted `req.body` and applies them to the `req.user` object without any filtering or allowlisting of which fields are permitted to be updated.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Explicitly define which fields are allowed to be updated from the request body (e.g., `const { bio, displayName } = req.body; Object.assign(req.user, { bio, displayName });`) instead of passing the entire body object.

findings_vulnerable.title: Hardcoded sensitive secrets in environment configuration
findings_vulnerable.summary: The file contains hardcoded secrets (`JWT_SECRET` and `PAYMENT_MERCHANT_KEY`) which are used for authentication and third-party service integration. Hardcoding secrets in configuration files that are likely to be committed to version control increases the risk of unauthorized access to user sessions and financial services.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The values `bakery-lab-jwt-3f9a1c7e5b2d` (line 3) and `mk_bakery_lab_7f3a9c2e1b8d4f60` (line 4) are static strings stored in a configuration file. If this file is committed to a repository, these secrets are compromised.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Move sensitive secrets to a dedicated secret management system (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) or use environment variables that are injected at runtime and never committed to version control.

findings_vulnerable.title: Potential Arbitrary File Read
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `load_branch_settings` function opens a file at the provided `path` without validating that the path is restricted to an expected directory.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The function `load_branch_settings` uses `open(path)` directly. If an attacker can control the `path` argument, they can read arbitrary files on the system.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Validate that the `path` is within an expected directory or use a whitelist of allowed files.

findings_vulnerable.title: Debug mode enabled in production-ready configuration
findings_vulnerable.summary: The application is configured to run with `debug=True` and listens on all network interfaces (`0.0.0.0`). Enabling debug mode in a non-development environment can lead to the exposure of sensitive source code, environment variables, and potentially allow arbitrary code execution via the interactive debugger.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Set `debug=False` for production environments and ensure the application binds to a specific, trusted interface (e.g., `127.0.0.1`) unless external access is explicitly required.

findings_vulnerable.title: Insecure JWT processing in attachUser
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `attachUser` function uses `jwt.decode` instead of `jwt.verify`. `jwt.decode` merely parses the payload without verifying the cryptographic signature. An attacker can provide a self-signed or unsigned JWT with a `sub` claim corresponding to any user, and the middleware will attach that user's data to the request, effectively allowing identity spoofing if other parts of the application rely on `req.user` for authorization.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Use `jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET)` instead of `jwt.decode(token)` to ensure the token's integrity and authenticity before trusting the claims.

findings_vulnerable.title: SQL Injection in search_orders
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `search_orders` endpoint interpolates the `customer` query parameter directly into a SQL query string, allowing for SQL injection.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The `term` variable is taken from `request.args.get("customer", "")` and used in an f-string within `db.execute` on line 40: `f"WHERE u.email LIKE '%{term}%' ORDER BY o.id DESC"`. An attacker can provide a malicious string to manipulate the query.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Use parameterized queries for the `LIKE` clause, for example: `db.execute("... WHERE u.email LIKE ? ...", (f"%{term}%",))`.

evidence.quote:
term = request.args.get("customer", "")
    rows = get_db().execute(
        "SELECT o.* FROM orders o JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id "
        f"WHERE u.email LIKE '%{term}%' ORDER BY o.id DESC"
    ).fetchall()

findings_vulnerable.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in get_order
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `get_order` endpoint allows any authenticated user to view any order by its ID, as it fails to verify that the order belongs to the requesting user.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: The function `get_order` retrieves an order by `order_id` but does not verify that `order["user_id"] == g.user["uid"]` before returning the data, unlike `cancel_order` which performs this check.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Add a check to ensure the order's `user_id` matches the `g.user["uid"]` before returning the order details.

findings_vulnerable.title: Negative quantity allows price manipulation in create_order
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `create_order` endpoint does not validate that the quantity of an item is a positive integer, allowing users to potentially manipulate the total price by providing negative quantities.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning: In `create_order`, `qty = int(line["qty"])` is performed on line 79, but there is no check to ensure `qty > 0`. A negative quantity would decrease the `total` calculated on line 80.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Validate that `qty` is a positive integer before proceeding with the calculation.

findings_vulnerable.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in product reviews
findings_vulnerable.summary: The `GET /products/:id` endpoint renders review text directly into the HTML response without escaping. Since the `POST /products/:id/reviews` endpoint allows any authenticated user to submit arbitrary text, an attacker can inject malicious scripts into a review that will execute in the browser of any user viewing the product page.
findings_vulnerable.reasoning:
In `storefront/src/routes/reviews.js`: Line 16: `.map((r) => `
  • ${escapeHtml(r.author)}: ${r.text}
    • `)` While `r.author` is escaped, `r.text` is concatenated directly into the template string. The data in `r.text` originates from `req.body.text` in the `POST` handler (line 26) and is never sanitized before being stored or rendered.
findings_vulnerable.remediation: Ensure that all user-provided content, including `r.text`, is passed through `escapeHtml()` before being rendered in the HTML response.
